solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: over = finished, as in 'the game is over'
an age = a period of time

annotation.surface: A journalist's story that was filed just before deadline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', which suits a report, but it is the Latin abbreviation c. for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the news sense: the coverage of an event is the body of reporting done on it.

indicatorNotes.purchasing: to purchase is to take something in exchange, so SHOTS takes the letter into itself
indicatorNotes.last: the final letter of the word before it, 'bar'

blocks.note: the second 'drinks' = shots, small measures of spirits

annotation.surface: Someone at closing time buying a final round at the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: The same word 'drinks' opens and closes the clue, once as definition and once as wordplay. In Britain shorts are spirits served in small measures, as opposed to long drinks like beer.
annotation.definitionFit: A British pub term: shorts are small servings of spirits, one kind of drinks, set against long drinks.

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of 'around', so THING is placed around RILL on both sides

blocks.note: a rill is a small stream or channel

annotation.surface: An item about a TV channel whose content is sensational.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but here it is a watercourse: a rill is a tiny stream.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sensational finish and a thrilling finish both excite the audience.

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: united = one, as in 'they were as one'
ROUSE (to start, startle) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A football team nearly getting their season started.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club name. 'Start' here is the verb meaning to startle or rouse, and 'trying' is an adjective, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: a trying job wears you down, as an onerous, burdensome one does.

entries.clue: Discards useless material, perhaps scrap initially (5)

annotation.definition: Discards useless material, perhaps scrap initially

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

annotation.surface: Someone clearing out junk that might be scrap.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: to throw out useless scrap is to dump it.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight as what someone who dumps things does: discarding useless material such as scrap.

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, the part below holds up the part above, so APACE goes under CAR

blocks.note: a Ferrari is an example of a car, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: A sports car's bodywork built for speed.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Ferrari as just one example of a car.
annotation.definitionFit: A zoological term: the carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle, crab or lobster.

indicatorNotes.catching: to catch something is to take hold of it, so PLACE closes around I

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: An angler's fish found in a spot where the current runs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' seems to belong with fish and water, but it is the electrical symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: plaice is a European flatfish, one kind of fish.

entries.clue: Fancy that game with empty stomach (4)

indicatorNotes.empty: an empty container has nothing inside, so the word keeps only its outside letters

annotation.surface: Surprise at someone playing sport on an empty stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that' is an exclamation of surprise, not a verb about liking something.
annotation.definitionFit: Two interchangeable exclamations: 'Gosh!' and 'Fancy that!' both express mild surprise.

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so ON sits within HOUR

blocks.note: a play is on when it is playing
an hour is a unit of time

annotation.surface: A musician playing in time, having practised properly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' is the adjective meaning morally correct, not a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the moral sense: doing the right thing is the honourable course.

entries.clue: Row follows judge being more generous (8)

indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come after, so TIER is placed after HEAR

blocks.note: a tier is a row of seats

annotation.surface: A courtroom row that ends with the judge being kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' could be an argument, but here it is a line of seats. 'Judge' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for portions or welcomes: a heartier helping is a more generous, ample one.

entries.clue: Still Caledonian’s first dressed in tartan (6)

indicatorNotes.dressed in: someone dressed in clothes is wrapped by them, so C is wrapped by PLAID

blocks.note: a plaid is a tartan cloth

annotation.surface: A Scot standing motionless in a kilt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'even now', but it is the adjective meaning calm. Caledonian means Scottish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for water or temperament: a still pond and a placid pond are both calm and unruffled.

entries.clue: Gold one found inside quiet tomb (9)

indicatorNotes.found inside: the letters are found inside, so AU and SOLE sit within MUM

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Treasure discovered in a silent burial chamber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' is the adjective meaning silent, as in 'mum's the word'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a mausoleum is a large, stately tomb, named after the tomb of King Mausolus.

indicatorNotes.not: not means without, so the T is left out

blocks.note: came to = obtained, reached, as a sum or result

annotation.surface: Someone got a minor role but not much money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obtained' is read as 'came to', the way a bill comes to a total.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre and film term: a cameo is a brief role, often played by a famous name.

entries.clue: Punch from barkeeper for a teetotaller (9)

indicatorNotes.from: from means taken out of, so the answer is lifted out of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the answer runs from the end of barkeeper into the start of teetotaller

annotation.surface: A teetotaller ordering a fruit punch from the barman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a drink, which suits the bar surface, but it is the verb meaning to make a hole.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to punch holes in paper is to perforate it.

annotation.surface: A wife worried her tough fabric is shrinking in the wash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shrinking' suggests laundry, but it is the tide going out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: webbing is tough woven strapping used for belts, harnesses and seat bases.

entries.clue: Rest beloved’s head, pretty embracing sweetheart (8)

annotation.type: charade + container + first letter + middle letter

indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to hug, so RATHER wraps around E
indicatorNotes.heart: the heart of a word is its middle letter

annotation.surface: A lover resting their head on a pretty sweetheart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is a classic trick: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter. 'Pretty' is the adverb, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal noun: taking a breather means stopping for a short rest to get your breath back.

entries.clue: Maybe dish out again for order (7)

blocks.note: to serve is one way to dish out food, hence 'maybe'

annotation.surface: A waiter serving seconds to a table.
annotation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer means to dish out again; read as one word it means to book ahead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the booking sense: to order a table or tickets in advance is to reserve them.

entries.clue: Batted, never getting upset about rivalry (8)

indicatorNotes.getting: getting means obtaining, so the answer is got out of the letters of the words
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

blocks.note: the letters run from after the B of batted to before the final ER of never

annotation.surface: A batsman never bothered by a bitter cricket rivalry.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of letters spans the comma; reading bATTED NEVer from bottom to top gives VENDETTA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by degree: a vendetta is a prolonged, bitter rivalry or feud, originally a blood feud between families.

entries.clue: Transparent material in glasses when delivered (7)

indicatorNotes.when delivered: a speech is delivered, so the words count by their sound when spoken

blocks.note: per = in (each), as in 'miles per hour'; specs = glasses

annotation.surface: Clear plastic lenses in spectacles arriving by post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests the postman, but it means spoken. Perspex is the British trade name for acrylic sheet, what Americans call Plexiglas.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade name used generically: Perspex is a clear acrylic plastic used in place of glass.

annotation.definitionNote: a taper is one who records on tape; the clue's past tense is loose
annotation.surface: A song recorded that became a hit alongside the rock band Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' and 'Queen' suggest the rock band's chart hits, but hit is a light blow and Queen is the royal cipher.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense of the noun: read as TAPE + ER, a taper is someone who records on tape, not the thin candle.

entries.clue: Sailor on route to foreign parts (6)

annotation.surface: A sailor travelling on his way overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the sailor on top of the route, so the sailor comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb of direction: travelling abroad means going to foreign parts, outside your own country.

entries.clue: Marine is fierce suppressing fear, oddly (9)

indicatorNotes.suppressing: to suppress is to hold something down within, so SEARING keeps FA inside it
indicatorNotes.oddly: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third

annotation.surface: A soldier in the Marines fighting to overcome his fear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning to do with the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: a marine nation and a seafaring nation both live by the sea.

blocks.note: the surface reading is to review or count up, like a shop doing an inventory; the meant reading is to steal livestock
stock that belongs to someone else, which turns taking it into theft

annotation.surface: Someone assessing how other people are getting on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stock' means livestock, and taking other people's cattle is rustling. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: to rustle is to steal cattle or horses, literally taking other people's stock.

indicatorNotes.revolting: to revolt originally meant to roll back, so the letters roll round the other way

annotation.surface: A critic dismissing a disgusting performance as rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, which suits a bad review, but it tells you to turn the letters around.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatrical synonym named after Thespis, the first Greek actor: a thespian is an actor.

entries.clue: Amorous heart accepting sex appeal returned (6)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take something in, so CORE takes IT inside
indicatorNotes.returned: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the core is the heart of something

annotation.surface: A lover whose feelings of desire are reciprocated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like love being returned, but it reverses the whole assembly.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: amorous and erotic both describe sexual desire, erotic leaning more to arousal.

indicatorNotes.flipped: flipping something over turns it the other way round

blocks.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, one kind of dessert

annotation.surface: Someone under pressure who has lost their temper at idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fools' are not idiots but a British pudding of fruit folded into cream, so 'possibly' marks them as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: someone under pressure at work feels stressed.

indicatorNotes.dropping: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the word loses a letter

annotation.surface: An aggressive man who drops someone in a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' is the Roman numeral I, removed from the middle of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a malevolent look is hostile, carrying ill will.

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as reported, spoken aloud, so the sound counts

annotation.surface: News that someone is ruining a musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb meaning ruins, but it is the noun meaning plunder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lute is a pear-shaped stringed instrument, plucked like a guitar.
